title: Adaptivity, Anchoring, and the Exact Oracle Complexity of Stochastic Fixed-Point Iterations
summary: We study stochastic fixed-point iterations $x_{n+1}=θ_nx_0+(1-θ_n)\widehat T(x_n)$ for nonexpansive and contractive operators on Hilbert spaces, with a single-point unbiased oracle of bounded variance. Deterministically, every anchor schedule $θ_n=c_n/(n+2)$ whose density $c_n\in(0,1]$ does not oscillate between scales is either polynomially suboptimal on contractions or super-polynomially slow on rotations; for constant densities $θ_n=c/(n+2)$ the tradeoff is exact, with $\norm{x_n}\asympΓ(c+1)(n\varphi)^{-c}$ on rotations by angle $\varphi$ ($\varphi\to0$, $n\varphi\to\infty$) and, for the…
